title: Gene regulatory network models exhibit associative learning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gene regulatory network models exhibit associative learning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Analyses of biological gene regulatory network models show that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning, as well as pattern completion and generalization, suggesting GRNs could be trained with patterned stimuli rather than rewired.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Indeed, recent analyses of biological GRN models reveal that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning capacity, as well as pattern completion and generalization (Watson et al., 2010, 2014; Szilagyi et al., 2020; Biswas et al., 2021).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences”. Scope: Published ODE models of biological gene regulatory networks

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Associative response, completion, and generalization can be given explicit simulation criteria. Public model repositories and published equations allow a small team to reproduce the model-level claim, though interpretation as learning remains somewhat contested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run published GRN models through prespecified conditioning, pattern-completion, and generalization protocols, comparing post-training responses with unpaired-stimulus and parameter-shuffled controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Learning terminology may map imperfectly onto dynamical adaptation.

Some cited models or parameters may require reconstruction from articles.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.86
data existence: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The models themselves are public, in Cell Collective and BioModels, and a later ODE analysis has open code, so a defined pairing protocol can be re-run. The flagship Boolean analysis did not release its code, and the cited papers do not share one decision rule. A new screen can test learning capacity in the published models and will not automatically reproduce each cited result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On published GRN models, pair a cue with an outcome-producing stimulus and test whether the cue later changes the response relative to unpaired controls; associative learning, pattern completion, or generalization holds if the paired network meets that criterion and a shuffled network does not.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Code for the 2021 Boolean memory screen was withheld, so the exact published runs cannot be replayed.

Associative learning, pattern completion, and generalization are defined differently across the cited papers.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.6
